missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-measure-extension-C008 (partial): The construction or argument owed under proved=annex:p15.stieltjes-construction is not written out in full. The endpoint-limit step proves only the lower end, that inf F is the limit at minus infinity. The upper end is dismissed with 'The upper-end proof is the reversed argument' (handbook/annex/p15/measure-extension.tex line 296), which is a 'similarly' in place of written steps. That upper-end fact, F(infinity) = sup F as the limit at plus infinity including the infinite case, is needed later for targets with right endpoint infinity (annex lines 383-385). Second, the stated conclusion 'Its values on bounded intervals are finite' (body handbook/parts/p15/measure-extension.tex lines 211-212) is never proved for bounded intervals other than the finite-endpoint members I(a,b). The monotonicity step from containment in some (-n,n] is not written (annex lines 401-411).

ED26-P15-CH-measure-extension-C012 (partial): The construction or argument owed under proved=annex:p15.cdf-existence depends on an unstated assumption. The theorem concludes that the law of Q_F equals mu_F and that it is the unique Borel probability law with cumulative function F (body lines 297-299). For this the proof (handbook/annex/p15/measure-extension.tex lines 512-516) cites thm:p15-cdf-laws. That theorem's statement covers only two real random variables (handbook/parts/p15/measurable-probability.tex lines 443-444), and the handbook defines a CDF only for a real random variable (lines 417-425). mu_F, and any Borel probability measure with the same ray values, is never shown to be the law of a real random variable, for example the identity map on (R, B(R), mu_F). No direct argument on the ray pi-system or via the Stieltjes uniqueness clause is written either. So the equality-of-laws and uniqueness conclusions lack a written step.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-product-measures-C013 (partial): The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.absolute-iterated-series is not supplied. The series half of the proof connects the corollary's sums to Fubini's integrals only through two bare assertions. The first is 'The assumed sum is the first iterated absolute integral, because integration with respect to kappa is summation' (handbook/annex/p15/product-measures.tex 514-515). The second is 'counting-measure integration of that integrable section equals the sum' (519-521). Neither identity is derived in this proof or established anywhere on the route: the integral against counting measure on N+ of a nonnegative g equals the sum of g(n), and the signed version holds for an absolutely summable section. The closest result, thm:p15-expectation-law-integral (handbook/parts/p15/integration-expectation.tex 324-348), gives the sum formula only for countable atomic probability spaces. Three identifications are therefore unwritten: the hypothesis sum of the integrals of |f_n| with Fubini's premise, H with the section absolute integral (516-518), and S with Fubini's second section-integral function (522-523). All other parts of C013 (the Tonelli criterion at 499-504, product measurability of F, the absolute-convergence bound, integrability of each f_n) are written.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-conditional-expectation-C002 (partial): The construction or argument is not written in full. In annex:p15.conditional-existence (handbook/annex/p15/conditional-expectation.tex lines 23-31) P is restricted to G and the proved Radon-Nikodym theorem is applied on (Omega,G,P|_G). That gives nu_pm(A) = int_A Z_pm d(P|_G). Lines 32-39 then say Z_pm are integrable with integrals EX^pm and write int_A Z dP = nu_+(A) - nu_-(A). This quietly swaps P|_G-integrals of G-measurable functions for P-integrals. No step or citation supports that swap, and no handbook result states it. It would follow from thm:p15-expectation-law-integral applied to the identity map (Omega,F0)->(Omega,G), or from G-simple approximation (thm:p15-measurable-limits) plus monotone convergence on both spaces. As written, the argument that the constructed Z satisfies the P-integral identity and P-integrability required by def:p15-general-conditional-expectation has an unwritten step. Every other element is present: integrability and E|Z|<=E|X| (annex 5-14), a.e. uniqueness (15-21), the source's X+/X- construction (23-39; Durrett p. 207, PDF 215), no completion (41), and the worked a.e.-uniqueness boundary (body 365-371, annex 727-739).

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P16-CH-measurable-causal-graphs-C002 (partial): The status is proved=annex:p16.measurable-ci-calculus, but the full proof is missing for the clause 'Measurable functions may be applied to either independent tuple, also using the conditioning tuple as an argument' (body measurable-causal-graphs.tex 47-48). Its only argument is a one-clause sketch at annex 53-56: 'by pushing forward the conditional product kernels at each z'. Nothing shows that the regular conditional law of (g(X,Z),h(Y,Z)) given Z=z is the image of the conditional product law at z. The substitution identity of thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure that would give this is neither used nor cited, and the proof never returns from that identity to the product-test definition. The Z-free case, both equivalences and the four semigraphoid properties are fully argued.

ED26-P16-CH-measurable-causal-graphs-C005 (partial): The status is proved=annex:p16.measurable-kernel-randomization, but the full proof is missing for the 'Consequently' assertion (body 90-94): every finite standard Borel kernel model has a representation X_v=F_v(X_pa(v),U_v) with mutually independent uniform U_v. Annex 157-160 says only 'Topological evaluation and successive conditioning show that its joint law is the kernel law'. It does not show that U_v is independent of the predecessors already constructed, that K_v(X_pa(v),.) is therefore their conditional law, or that induction identifies the joint law with P_K. The matching argument later at annex 508-513 is not invoked. The single-kernel realization (112-155) and the non-uniqueness example (160-166) are complete.

ED26-P16-CH-measurable-causal-graphs-C010 (partial): The status is proved=annex:p16.measurable-response-component, but the full proof is missing for the stated consequence (body 304-307): one conditional product law of (R,B) given C licenses integration of the whole family at a measurable random parameter depending on (B,C). Annex 567-573 is a two-sentence sketch. It does not derive L(R|B,C)=L(R|C) as kernels from R independent of B given C, and it does not substitute the random parameter into F via thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure. Separately, annex 537-538 ('by the separation hypothesis') relies, without stating or citing them, on two facts: exposing private roots preserves d-separation (stated only later, at 580-581) and the moral-separation bridge. The pointwise representation and R independent of B given C are argued (545-565).

ED26-P16-CH-measurable-causal-graphs-C012 (partial): The status is proved=annex:p16.measurable-mediation-fields, but the proof of item 1 (body 364-365) is incomplete. In the cross-world field, annex 610-611 claims 'The mediator tuple in this auxiliary model is exactly M_b, by topological evaluation on its restored ancestors'. For that, every exposure child that is an ancestor of a mediator must lie outside D_Y; annex 607-608 gives exposure input a to every exposure child in D_Y. The listed 'exact graph facts' (594-605) put into D_M only the heads of restored edges and their parents. No step places the other exposure children among the mediator ancestors in D_M, so the construction of M_b, and with it R_0 independent of M_b given C, is not fully argued. The claim at 613-615 that every vertex needed for Y belongs to D_Y is likewise only asserted. Items 2 and 3 and the reference-mediator law are argued.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-regular-conditional-laws-C002 (partial): The worked boundary is missing for this entry. def:p15-regular-conditional-law (handbook/parts/p15/regular-conditional-laws.tex lines 49-51) says the regular-conditional-probability special case (S=Omega, target sigma-algebra F_0, X the identity) 'needs an existence hypothesis on the outcome space itself'. That is, it claims a regular conditional law need not exist unless (Omega,F_0) satisfies some hypothesis. Nothing on the handbook route shows this. No probability space and sub-sigma-algebra G are given for which no probability kernel from (Omega,G) to (Omega,F_0) satisfies the defining identities, and no argument for the necessity is written. The only support is the citation at conditioning-independence-and-information-w02b-p15-008.tex lines 235-239. It points to Durrett p. 214 (PDF p. 222), which says such laws do not always exist and credits Dieudonne (1948) without giving the example. That is a citation where a demonstration is owed. The countable-cocountable model (w02b-p15-008 annex lines 171-269) does not fill the gap: it shows a source-sense law that cannot be repaired, but a regular conditional law still exists in that model. Owed: a written model in which no regular conditional probability exists, with its proof, or a written argument that establishes the stated need for a hypothesis.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-feller-bernstein-hausdorff-C016 (partial): The hypotheses are not plainly stated. Body line 345 reads 'positive black weight b, red weight r and same-color reinforcement c>0'. That wording puts a positivity condition on b and c but none on the red weight r. The conclusion that the c_n are 'precisely the moments of beta(b/c,r/c)', which Hausdorff uniqueness then uses to identify the mixing law, needs r>0. The handbook defines beta(alpha,beta) only for alpha,beta>0 (def:p15-beta-integral), and the cited exchangeability theorem thm:p15-polya-word-law assumes r>0. At r=0 the formula gives c_n=1, which are the moments of delta_1, and no beta law exists. So r>0 is an unstated assumption on the plain reading. Every other element is present: the product and gamma forms of c_n, the empty-product convention, the beta moments, the Hausdorff identification, the word and count probabilities, and agreement with the direct urn law (body 344-358, annex 555-584, held Feller II PDF pp. 244-245 = printed 229-230).

missing_pieces.duty: assessment_dispute: US-0: Item (6) of thm:p15-w02b-p15-013-comparison (handbook/parts/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02b-p15-013.tex lines 215-220) claims an 'if and only if': X_n->X in probability and in L^p iff X_n in L^p for every n and (|X_n|^p) is uniformly integrable. The annex proof (handbook/annex/p15/limit-theorems-and-concentration-w02b-p15-013.tex lines 198-199) only cites thm:p15-w02b-p15-013-vitali, which already assumes X_n in L^p (parts line 231). The necessity of X_n in L^p and of uniform integrability is never argued. It is also false under the chapter's own definition (parts lines 77-78, 85-88): take X_n=X=Y with E|Y|^p=infinity; this converges in L^p and in probability, yet X_n is not in L^p and |X_n|^p is not uniformly integrable. So the named probability-to-mean comparison is not established as stated. All 70 MP/UI/WCL components and the rest of the comparison (three ranges, L^p inside L^q, a.s./probability/distribution implications, general-p Vitali, five countermodels, the 12-pair failure count, and the Durrett variants checked in the held PDF) are covered.

In the held source (Durrett v5, PDF p.151, book p.143) that exercise asks for two things: show nu_k^{1/k} -> lambda, "so the assumption of Theorem 3.3.26 holds if lambda < infinity". The body and the annex proof (annex 1038-1077) prove only nu_k^{1/k} -> Lambda (annex 1040-1052, including nu_k^{1/k} <= Lambda) and, separately, compact Hamburger determinacy by polynomial approximation (annex 1054-1075). No line states or derives that the growth hypothesis of thm:p15-criteria-moment-method / thm:p15-criteria-analytic-determinacy (limsup m_{2k}^{1/(2k)}/(2k) < infinity) holds when Lambda < infinity. missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C001 (partial): Hypotheses and source variant are not supplied (failure condition: unstated assumption). def:p15-filtration-martingale (body 18-26) defines adaptedness but never requires it. A martingale is therefore any real process with integrable terms and E(X_{n+1}|F_n)=X_n, and sub/supermartingales swap the identity for an inequality. The held source's definition (Durrett PTE5 p. 217) has three conditions, and condition (ii), 'X_n adapted to F_n', is dropped. For sub- and supermartingales the inequality does not imply adaptedness. The handbook's own proofs still rely on it: annex 77 says 'The case n=m follows from adaptedness', annex 91 says 'adaptedness was explicitly assumed', and annex 35/104/124/150/412/559/586/734 check adaptedness. The optional-stopping chapter on the same route states the convention outright (optional-stopping-and-random-walks.tex 12-13). Concrete case: take F_n trivial, X_0=-2-U and X_n=-1 for n>=1. This meets the definition as written, but the n=m case of thm:p15-martingale-conditioning fails.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C003 (partial): Promised cases are not written. Body 72-74 promises the reduced-filtration property for all three classes. The annex writes only the supermartingale chain (annex 84-89). The submartingale and martingale cases are dispatched with 'The sign-reversed and equality cases are identical with their respective signs' (annex 90-91). That is a 'similarly'-type deferral, with no written steps and no formal reduction such as the X -> -X reduction used at annex 78. The multi-step inequality, mean monotonicity and natural-filtration parts are written.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C006 (partial): (1) Unstated assumption. The first assertion, 'For predictable bounded H_i, the transform is adapted and integrable at every finite time' (body 107-108), places no hypothesis on X. Its proof needs X adapted and integrable at each time (annex 144-150). Compare body 135-136, where the analogous X_T claim states exactly these hypotheses. (2) The promised submartingale case for H_i>=0 (body 111-112) gets only 'The submartingale case uses the opposite sign' (annex 160). The martingale and supermartingale cases are written.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C007 (partial): Unsupported source attribution. The stopped information F_T (body 118-122) is attributed only through the chapter statement at body 9-10: 'The source for the constructions, theorems and exercises developed here is Durrett's Section 4.2', pp. 217-224. Those pages of the held source define a stopping time by {N=n} in F_n (p. 220) and contain no stopped sigma-field. The source first uses F_M in Ex. 4.4.3-4.4.4 (p. 239). The stopping-time and stopped-process parts are supported by p. 220.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C008 (partial): Unsupported source attribution. Three assertions are attributed by body 9-10 to Durrett Section 4.2, pp. 217-224: F_T is a sigma-algebra, S<=T implies F_S is contained in F_T, and X_T is F_T-measurable and integrable for bounded T (body 132-136; annex 173-200). Those pages contain only the {N=n} stopping-time definition and Theorem 4.2.9 (p. 220), with no stopped sigma-field. The {T=n} equivalence and stopped-process preservation are written and supported by the source.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C009 (partial): (1) Unsupported source attribution. The entry (E(X_T|F_S)=X_S and its inequalities for S<=T<=N, body 145-156) is attributed only by body 9-10 to Durrett Section 4.2, pp. 217-224. No bounded-time sampling theorem and no stopped sigma-field appear on those pages; in the held source this material is Thm 4.4.1 (p. 235) and Ex. 4.4.2-4.4.4 (pp. 238-239). (2) The promised submartingale case is dispatched by 'The submartingale case reverses the inequalities' (annex 243). (3) The step from 'the integral of X_T over A <= the integral of X_S over A, for every A in F_S' to E(X_T|F_S)<=X_S is not written here. It is handed off to 'the bounded-level conditional comparison argument' (annex 239-240). That is a technique written for pointwise order at annex/p15/conditional-expectation.tex 115-127, not a stated result.

ED26-P15-CH-martingales-and-convergence-C011 (partial): Unstated assumption. The alternating times are defined for an arbitrary real process (body 161-168). The entry's first assertion, that the T_j are stopping times and H_m is predictable (body 185-186), comes before and independently of the submartingale hypothesis at body 189. It holds only for adapted X, and its proof uses adaptedness: annex 255 ({T_1<=n} = union of {X_m<=a}, in F_n) and annex 258-260. The held source states this construction for a submartingale (p. 220). The greedy-maximality and clipped-process inequality parts are written.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-optional-stopping-and-random-walks-C009 (partial): Hypotheses not supplied: an unstated assumption. The statement of Wald's second identity (handbook/parts/p15/optional-stopping-and-random-walks.tex lines 174-179) asserts that S_{T and n} -> S_T in L2 and ES_T^2 = sigma^2 ET for any T with ET<infinity. It never says T is a stopping time. Every other sampling entry in the chapter does declare it, at lines 48, 65, 79, 97, 119, 162 and 195. The held source's Exercise 4.8.4 (Durrett v5, printed p. 261 = PDF p. 269) states 'if T is a stopping time with ET<infinity'. The annex proof relies on the property without stating it: annex line 186 uses that {T>=j} is F_{j-1}-measurable. The source hypothesis is therefore not preserved. The omission matters: with fair signs, let T=1 on {xi_1=xi_2} and T=2 otherwise. Then ES_T^2 = 1/2, but sigma^2 ET = 3/2. The exit-time bound, its strict form and the sigma^2=0 case are present.

ED26-P15-CH-optional-stopping-and-random-walks-C020 (partial): The construction or argument is not fully written. To prove E_x tau<infinity, the annex chooses delta>0 with P(xi_1>=delta)>0 (handbook/annex/p15/optional-stopping-and-random-walks.tex line 597). That requires ruling out xi_1<=0 a.s. The text argues only the case xi_1>=0 a.s., which the proof never uses. The case it does use is dismissed as 'the nonpositive case is analogous' (line 595), which counts as a 'similarly' step in an owed proof. Three results depend on this finiteness: the overshoot integrability E_x e^{theta S_tau} <= e^{theta a} E_x tau (line 628), the exact identity E_x e^{theta_0 S_tau} = e^{theta_0 x} (lines 629-630) and the lower-exit bound. The one-sided bound for the possibly infinite T (lines 635-646) does not depend on it.

The annex (handbook/annex/p15/density-martingales-and-product-measures.tex l.362-363) derives that assertion only from 'the affinity series criterion and its reverse-measure conclusion'. (ii) The claimed singularity for eps_m=1/(4 sqrt m) rests on the words 'giving the two examples', with no written step sum(1-h_m)=infinity => H_infinity=0 => mu perp nu. The Poisson and gamma conclusions are asserted for positive real n tending to infinity (body 40-41, 53-56; annex 38-39, 50). ED26-P15-CH-feller-bernstein-hausdorff-C016 (partial): Worked boundary not supplied. The entry's only edge content is the notational convention that the empty product is one (body 354). Those hypotheses are positive weights b and r and reinforcement c>0, on which the beta(b/c, r/c) identification depends.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-polya-urns-and-beta-prediction-C007 (partial): The full proof promised by proved=annex:p15.polya-posterior-prediction is not completely written. Annex lines 175-182 assert that every future indicator has conditional mean a/T and variance ab/T^2, and that every distinct future pair has conditional joint success probability a(a+1)/(T(T+1)). They then add these to get E(K_{n,m}|F_n)=ma/T and Var(K_{n,m}|F_n)=mab(T+m)/(T^2(T+1)). The written argument (lines 167-173) only gives the conditional probability of a specified future word. It never derives the conditional marginal of B_{n+j} for j>=2 or of a non-adjacent pair: no conditional exchangeability of the future given the past, no marginalization over intermediate draws, no martingale step, and no appeal to the conditional Bernoulli product of thm:p15-polya-beta-limit. The conditional mean and variance of K_{n,m}, and the m>1 excess over mX_n(1-X_n), therefore rest on a step that is asserted but not proved.

ED26-P15-CH-polya-urns-and-beta-prediction-C009 (partial): The entry does not preserve the identified source variant, although every mathematical clause is stated and proved (annex 239-280). The held source (Durrett PTE5, printed p. 227, PDF p. 235) displays the unscaled cell probability P(G_n=m+2)=[n!/(m!(n-m)!)][(m+1)!(n-m)!/((n+2)!/2)] -> 2x for c=1, g=2, r=1. The entry states nP(G_n=s_n+2)->2x and P(G_n=s_n+2)->0 (body 192-197, annex 272-279) and says the annex 'retains the source's direct finite-mass route to both limits' (body 198). Neither the entry, its annex, nor def:p15-polya-source-scope records the source's own reading or that the factor n corrects it. The held text contains neither the scaled limit nor P->0, so it does not support crediting the source with a route to both stated limits.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-BM-RAT2021-4-1-C05 (partial): The component must account for every promised proof or evidence claim in the selected extent and fix the finite dependent-source set; empirical claims must keep their study/task/population/uncertainty and conflict boundaries. The fixed set is tab:p15-w02b-p15-022-dependent-sources, rows D1-D21 with D5a and D8a. Its stated scope (022 lines 668-670 and 848-849) is limited to claims the survey reports as established elsewhere, which is narrower than every claim in the extent. Two kinds of claim are not accounted for anywhere on the route. (i) The survey's own empirical and historical evidence claims: that the Brier score is used in practice to score weather forecasters and political analysts (p. 242); that Lewis's 1994 formulation is how the Principal Principle is usually understood and that the literature overlooks the change of formulation (p. 243); and that formal epistemology is a leading growth area in which Bayesian approaches dominate (p. 247). These are omitted rather than given an evidential status, so none keeps a study/task/population/uncertainty or conflict boundary. (ii) The claim at rationality-4-1.tex lines 216-222, that the accuracy argument needs one specific strictly proper measure, depends on Bronfman (manuscript), cited on p. 242 and listed on p. 249. Bronfman is missing from the fixed dependent-source set.

ED26-METHOD-maximum-entropy-C03 (partial): Normalization and the multiplier equations are explained without presupposing a feasible optimizer (043 lines 103-153 and 296-345), and the worked distributions solve their declared problems. The component's required extent, however, is the complete construction in the original paper including its constraint and normalization derivations, and two of Jaynes's multiplier derivations are absent. (a) Jaynes's (2-15) (p. 623), the maximum-entropy estimate of the parameter derivatives of the constraint functions, equal to -(1/lambda_r) times the parameter derivative of ln Z, is not stated or derived. The forces in (3-4) rest on it. (b) Jaynes's (5-1)-(5-3) (p. 627) are absent: they make lambda_k the integrating factor of the generalized heat dQ_k and the quantity statistically conjugate to f_k, and (5-8) (p. 628) gives lambda = dS/d<E> = 1/T. Neither 166.6 nor 166.7 states, under the hypotheses of thm:p15-w02b-p15-043-existence, how the maximal entropy v_nu(c) changes with the declared values. So the source's interpretation of the multipliers is neither given nor made conditional on its premises. Only the identification lambda_1 = 1/kT appears (043 line 484).

ED26-METHOD-maximum-entropy-C04 (partial): The inferential interpretation is made conditional on the reconstructed premises (J1)-(J5) (043 lines 401-479). Those are not the paper's complete inferential argument and stated premises, which the component's required extent demands. Neither 166.6 nor 166.7 mentions ergodicity, metric transitivity or equal a priori probabilities. Missing: (a) the paper's thesis that statistical mechanics, read as inference, needs no ergodicity, metric transitivity or equal a priori probabilities (pp. 620, 621, 627, 629). Also missing are its premise that the laws of motion add no information about the state beyond what measurement supplied, and its argument that new integrals of motion, or proof that a system is not metrically transitive, would give no rational basis for excluding states the information allows unless new data are added (pp. 624-625). (b) The normative claim that maximum-entropy estimates are justified independently of experimental verification and remain the best estimates the information permits, whether or not they agree with experiment (pp. 620, 626). The interpretation is therefore conditional on an incomplete statement of the source's premises.

The paper's own stated justificatory claims are missing, so the interpretation is not shown to be conditional on all the premises the paper states. The paper argues this from three points: the laws of motion add no information beyond measurement; there is no rational basis for excluding any state the information allows, which acts like an ergodic hypothesis whether or not the system is ergodic; and the conclusion section reaches the usual relations without ensembles or ergodic arguments (abstract; p. 621 'reversal'; p. 623; pp. 624-625; p. 627; p. 629); (iii) inventing a fictitious ensemble cannot change the subjective standing of the probabilities (p. 626). None of these appears in 043/044 or anywhere else on the route, yet 043 lines 704-709 present Sections 1-6 as the treated extent. The required extent is the complete inferential argument of the original paper, so the reconstruction is incomplete.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-bayes-factor-computation-C004 (partial): The success condition requires the entry's hypotheses to be supplied, and the failure condition 'unstated assumption' holds. The lemma thm:p15-laplace-curvature-replacement (body 122-138) states only these hypotheses: F_n=nJ_n with J_n symmetric and eigenvalues >= c, ||J~_n-J_n|| <= delta_n < c/2, and the mode, likelihood and prior ordinate held fixed. Those hypotheses support only the bound |log Î(F~_n)/Î(F_n)| <= d delta_n/c. The entry also concludes that 'delta_n=O(n^-1/2) gives relative error O(n^-1/2)', that 'O(n^-1) preserves that smaller error order', and that expected information may be substituted. These are relative errors against I_n, so they need Î(F_n)/I_n=1+O(n^-1), which holds only under the MLE Laplace hypotheses of thm:p15-laplace-mode-variants / def:p15-laplace-family. The lemma never states those hypotheses. The annex proof ends (lines 106-109) by 'multiplication by the already proved 1+O(n^-1) approximation', which is proved only under them. The companion boundary theorem has to verify them separately (annex 391-393).

ED26-P15-CH-bayes-factor-computation-C005 (partial): The statement (body 430-459) is present and its annex proof (113-132) is written out. The worked boundaries are also present: the BIC-to-exact ratio tends to 2, and the unit-information instance works. The element 'preserve the identified source variants' is not met, and the failure condition 'unsupported source attribution' holds at the component's Sec. 4.1.3 locator. (a) Body 471-473 attributes 'Different blockwise information rates, singular curvature, boundary modes and increasing dimension require other results' to \cite[Sec.~4.1.3]. The held source's Sec. 4.1.3 (pp. 778-779) covers only n as the Hessian growth rate and two-stage hierarchical models. Boundary modes are in Sec. 4.1.2 (Hsiao 1994, p. 778), large degrees of freedom are in Sec. 4.4 (p. 781), and singular curvature appears nowhere in Sec. 4. (b) The 'before discarding terms' display and the remark that 'both prior-log terms have coefficient two' (body 461-469) differ from the source's printed eq. (6) (p. 778), which gives those terms coefficient one. The text never identifies the printed variant, although it does flag the printed eq. (12) explicitly at body 647-651. (c) Two source variants at this locator are not presented. The source states (9), (S - log B12)/log B12 -> 0, without any condition; the handbook gives it only as its own conditional clause, with no attribution. Jeffreys's S + c with a Cauchy-prior constant (p. 779; the source calls it 'Jeffreys's variant' of the Schwarz criterion on p. 781) does not appear anywhere in the chapter.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C008 (partial): The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.binomial.most.powerful is not supplied. The argument that no level-1/2 test is most powerful against both p=1/4 and p=3/4 writes out only the p=3/4 maximization (annex 264-269). The p=1/4 half is waved through as 'the reversed calculation' (annex 270-272), a similarly-type appeal in place of the owed step. That half is: power (3/4)a+(1/4)b=(1/4)(a+b)+(1/2)a <= 3/4 under a+b <= 1, with equality only at a=1, b=0.

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C013 (partial): The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.neyman.interval.construction is not supplied. The proof needs a finite upper endpoint u(x) to belong to S(x), both for S(x)=[l(x),u(x)] intersected with R and for the upper-endpoint case of the source's Proposition VII (Neyman 1937 p. 355). That step is waved through with 'The same argument puts a finite u in S(x)' (annex 445-446). Only the lower-endpoint argument is written (annex 439-444).

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C016 (partial): The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.binomial.confidence.coverage is not supplied. The upper-endpoint half of the exact inversion is waved through with 'Similarly ... for k=n, both are false' (annex 593-600). That half is p > u_n(k) iff F_{n,p}(k) < d for k<n, from F decreasing strictly with F_{n,u_n(k)}(k)=d, plus both conditions failing at k=n because u_n(n)=1 and F_{n,p}(n)=1>d. Both the inversion claim and the coverage bound of at least 1-alpha (annex 609-621) depend on this unwritten half.

ED26-P15-CH-hypothesis-tests-and-confidence-C017 (partial): The full treatment promised by the declared status proved=annex:p15.binomial.beta.quantiles is not supplied. The upper-limit formula u_n(k)=Q_{k+1,n-k}(1-d) depends on the lower-tail identity F_{n,p}(k)=1-I_p(k+1,n-k) for k<n. That identity is only asserted with 'Likewise' (annex 690-694). Neither route to it is written: F_{n,p}(k)=1-T_{n,p}(k+1) combined with the upper-tail identity at k+1, or derivative matching with value 1 at p=0. Only the upper-tail identity behind the lower-limit formula is derived (annex 677-689).

Its exact claim sup_{R in H_1} E_R N_{a,b} = E_{Q_1} N_{a,b} = (1-(3/5)^r)/(2/5) and the annex argument (annex 486-514: 'its mass p at one ranges over [2/5,3/5]'; 'If no such observation has occurred by time r, the test exits at the lower boundary') hold only when the space is {0,1}. R lies in H_1, and at a=3c it gives P_R(N>3)=19/125>0. Hence E_R N >= 264/125 > 49/25 = E_{Q_1} N. The failure condition 'unstated assumption' holds. Owed: state X={0,1} (or restrict H to laws on {0,1}) as a hypothesis of the entry, or compute and prove the worst-case expected size over the full stated alternative class.

ED26-P15-CH-robust-hypothesis-testing-C008 (partial): Item 3 claims 'Such a choice exists, including the possible zero-risk singular case', and the declared proof does not prove this with written steps. Annex lines 313-321 restate a general bracketing fact for quantiles and support it only with 'This follows directly from the inverse-CDF construction in the preceding proof, or from the same continuity argument as thm:p15-likelihood-threshold'. That is a pointer standing in for the derivation. The cited lemma is stated and proved for P_0 with a likelihood ratio that is finite P_0-almost surely, not for the mixture M=L_0Q_0^n+L_1Q_1^n, under which T_n can carry an infinite atom. The steps in def:p15-occam-method (handbook/parts/p15/occam-learning.tex lines 251-255) never require that the m training observations be independent draws with the population law P. That is the hypothesis of def:p15-occam-model at lines 20-21, and item 1 of thm:p15-occam-boundaries (lines 213-216) shows the guarantee fails without it. Even so, the conclusion at lines 257-258 claims 'the stated probability over the sample'. The steps also never require fixing a target-size bound n with l(f) <= n, which puts the target in the fixed represented class. The 'required output-size' bound n^c m^a (line 130) depends on n, and so do the sample sizes of thm:p15-occam-compression (lines 147-151) and thm:p15-occam-minimum-approximation (lines 171-173). As written, 'choose the sample size from the applicable theorem' cannot be carried out from the listed steps. The method lists the learner-side premises and the fixed-before-sampling premise as explicit steps but leaves out these data-side premises. The sibling methods do state the sampling assumption: def:p15-conc-reference-method (bounded-concentration-learning.tex 444-445) and def:p15-w02b-p15-064-method (statistical-learning-and-generalization-w02b-p15-064.tex 362-363).

The entry calls itself the source's Lemmas 2--3 (handbook/parts/p15/huber-robust-location.tex line 60). It omits the source's Remark to Lemma 3 (Huber 1964, printed p.77, PDF p.5). That Remark lets the sign-change hypothesis on lambda be replaced by a weaker one: lambda exists and is finite at some xi_0 and does not vanish identically on a nondegenerate interval. ED26-P15-CH-huber-robust-location-C007 (partial): Source variant narrowed. The source's Winsorizing property (example (iii), printed p.79, PDF p.7) takes t_0 = T_n(x). It replaces each observation with |x_i - t_0| > k by the nearer of t_0 - k and t_0 + k, without changing the estimate T_n(x), and t_0 equals the modified mean. The entry (body 145-147) states only that, for any zero t_0, the score still vanishes at t_0 and t_0 is the modified mean. The annex (188-194) proves only that a minimizing location is preserved. It adds that the replacement 'need not preserve every tie-breaking rule for every modified sample'. The invariance of the estimate itself is neither stated nor proved: the modified sample's zero set is the single point t_0, so its midpoint estimate equals T_{n,k}(x).

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-GAP-SCI-002-C04 (partial): The success condition 'one order-of-magnitude estimate with input ranges and an omitted-variable failure' is met only by the 073 lane-capacity estimate (measurement-dimensional-constraints-and-approximate-inferenc-w02b-p15-073.tex lines 284-375). That estimate rests on source Section 1.2, pp. 6-7, as 073 itself says at lines 28-41 and 447-449. Section 1.2 is outside the required extent 'chapter 1 sections 1.3-1.5 only for the finite estimate example'. The in-extent finite estimates in the destination body (dimensional-and-scaling-inference.tex lines 566-608: the Sec. 1.3 bill-volume and train trees and the Sec. 1.4 oil imports) have no omitted-variable failure, and only the train tree has input ranges (3200-10800 per hour, not reported as an order of magnitude). The failure condition 'report unearned digits' also holds. The oil estimate is given as 'about 3.33 10^9 barrels per year' from one-significant-figure leaf values and set against a reported 3.34 billion (lines 599-603); the held source gives 3 x 10^9 (printed pp. 15-16). The flight-range order estimate, which the text says 'discards a factor of order two', is given as 'about 9.8 10^6 m' (lines 427-433); the held source gives about 10^7 m (eq. 4.86, printed p. 133).

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-GAP-SCI-008-C04 (partial): Half of the success condition is met: the warranted assignment contrast is stated, with its weights and premises and the unbiasedness theorem (factorial-inference-and-estimability.tex 677-726, annex 373-392; 077 404-466), and no failure condition holds. The other half, 'the additional premise for a mechanism claim', is not stated. Lines 736-741 list only kinds of evidence: process measurements with an explicit measurement model, and interventions or controls that separate the competing mechanisms. They add an unspecified category, 'assumptions connecting those observations to the causal equations', and say only that a mechanism interpretation has 'its own premises'. The passages at 075 656-662 and 077 449-450 just point back to that paragraph. Nowhere on the route is the premise itself given, meaning what must be assumed before the estimable assignment contrast can support the reflection-mechanism claim. An example would be that the checking instruction affects the response only through the reflection variable, which rules out the effort pathway of model two in thm:p15-factorial-mechanism. Another would be a stated mediation premise. The chapter promises at lines 12-13 to state 'the additional conditions under which an estimable contrast is ... an identified causal mechanism', but it delivers only a theorem that the mechanism is not identified. The route also has no link to the mediation premises in handbook/parts/p16/causal-mediation.tex.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-GAP-SCI-008-C04 (partial): The success condition requires stating the warranted assignment contrast and the additional premise for a mechanism claim. The first part is met: handbook/parts/p15/factorial-inference-and-estimability.tex 692-726 gives the weights (0,0,-1,1) and (-1,1,-1,1)/2 with the unbiased weighting estimator, and 077 404-466 lists the premises for the assignment contrast. The second part is not met. thm:p15-factorial-mechanism (728-734) proves that the factorial surface does not identify the reflection mechanism. The text then lists only kinds of further evidence plus unspecified 'assumptions connecting those observations to the causal equations' (736-741). The same deferral recurs without a premise at 077:449-450 ('needs the additional evidence'), 075:661-662 ('needs further premises again') and P19 evidence-methods.tex:667-670. No premise that would license a mechanism claim is ever stated. An example would be a structural restriction excluding the competing effort path that separates the theorem's two models, or a condition under which the reflection variable's intervention effect is identified. The chapter's own opening promise (lines 12-13) to state 'the additional conditions under which an estimable contrast is ... an identified causal mechanism' is therefore not delivered. The failure condition does not hold, because no coefficient is called proof of the mechanism.

missing_pieces.duty: ED26-METHOD-evidence-synthesis-C02 (partial): The success condition is met for the weights, heterogeneity and interval procedures. For two selected procedures, however, the claim that the stated dependence or common-effect assumption yields the stated conclusion is asserted rather than derived, because the owed proof steps are not written. (1) thm:p15-synthesis-linear (body lines 143-146) asserts that a_*^T Y +/- z sqrt(V_*) is an exact 1-alpha interval when Y is 'multivariate normal' with known general covariance. 'Multivariate normal' is not defined anywhere on the handbook route. Annex lines 52-55 prove normality of the weighted combination only for independent estimates (via thm:p15-normal-sums) and dispose of the dependent case with 'the covariance representation gives the general case', which is a sketch. (2) thm:p15-synthesis-table-delta (body lines 274-275) asserts that the Mantel-Haenszel risk-ratio estimate is consistent under a common risk ratio. Annex lines 149-150 discharge this 'by the same argument' without writing the risk-ratio limiting sums or the summand-ratio step, which is a 'similarly' step.
